questions.q: ​In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the sister of B’, A – B means ‘A is the husband of B’, A × B means ‘A is the mother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the brother of B’. Based on the above information, how is K related to O if ‘K + L – M × N ÷ O’?
questions.solution:
L is M’s husband and M is the mother of N and O. Thus L is O’s father. K is L’s sister, making her O’s paternal aunt.
**Answer: Father's sister**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘kids are playing’ is coded as ‘pu rs bp’ and ‘people love kids’ is coded as ‘rs gu xc’. How is ‘kids’ coded in that language?
questions.solution:
Kids is the only common word, and rs is the only common code between the two statements. Therefore kids is coded rs.
**Answer: rs**

questions.q: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 15, 29 32, 63
questions.solution:
The second number is twice the first minus one. The pair 17, 33 follows this rule because 2 × 17 - 1 = 33.
**Answer: 17, 33**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘LITE’ is coded as ‘1527’ and ‘EDIT’ is coded as ‘5124’. What is the code for ‘D’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
E, I and T occur in both words and share codes 5, 1 and 2. D occurs only in EDIT and takes the remaining code 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No elephant is a horse. No horse is a donkey. No horse is a turtle. Conclusions: (I) No elephant is a donkey. (II) Some turtles are donkeys.
questions.solution:
The statements only exclude horses from three groups. They do not fix relationships between elephants, donkeys and turtles. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.**

questions.q: FIBA is related to EJAB in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ZELU is related to YFKV. To which of the following is COIS related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Apply alternate shifts -1, +1, -1, +1 to the letters. COIS becomes BPHT.
**Answer: BPHT**

questions.q: D, E, F, G, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. T sits to the immediate left of S. U sits to the immediate left of D. D sits second to the left of G. E sits third to the left of S. Who sits fourth to the right of F?
questions.solution:
Fix S, then place T immediately left and E three left. The G–D–U positions fill the remaining seats and leave F in the final gap. G is fourth to F’s right.
**Answer: G**

questions.q: P, Q, R, S, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. E lives on floor number 4. Only two people live between E and R. Only P lives between E and Q. S lives immediately below E. Who lives on floor number 2?
questions.solution:
R occupies floor 1. E is on floor 4 and S directly below on 3. Q must be on 6 with P on 5 between Q and E. F is left for floor 2.
**Answer: F**

questions.q: If ‘+’ means ‘−’, ‘−’ means ‘×’, ‘×’ means ‘÷’, ‘÷’ means ‘+’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 57 − 7 ÷ 119 + 288 × 2 = ?
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? DCE 19 FEG 14 HGI 9 JIK 4 ?
questions.solution:
Every letter advances two positions while the number falls by five. The next term after JIK 4 is LKM -1.
**Answer: LKM -1**

questions.q: Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single-digit numbers only. (Left) 7 8 @ 1 # 4 $ 5 % + ? 8 & 6 % 4 8 9 % (Right) If all the symbols are dropped from the series, which of the following will be seventh from the right?
questions.solution:
After removing symbols, the sequence is 7, 8, 1, 4, 5, 8, 6, 4, 8, 9. Seventh from the right is the fourth from the left, namely 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: GOAT is related to IQCV in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, OWIB is related to QYKD. To which of the following options is UCOH related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Each letter moves two places forward in the alphabet. UCOH therefore becomes WEQJ.
**Answer: WEQJ**

questions.q: JELU is related to NHNV in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, BGMQ is related to FJOR. To which of the following is GKNP related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Apply successive shifts +4, +3, +2 and +1. GKNP changes to KNPQ.
**Answer: KNPQ**

questions.q: Each of the digits in the number 1847536 is arranged in the ascending order from left to right. The position of how many digits will remain unchanged as compared to that in the original number?
questions.solution:
The ascending order is 1345678. Only the first digit 1 and the third digit 4 stay in the same positions. Thus two digits remain unchanged.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: M, N, O, P, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it is numbered 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. E lives on the topmost floor. Only three people live between E and M. O lives on a floor below M. N lives on an even-numbered floor. P lives on an odd-numbered floor but not on floor number 5. How many people live between F and M?
questions.solution:
From floors 1 to 6 the residents are O, M, P, N, F, E. P and N live between M and F, giving two people.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: Seven people F, G, H, I, U, V, and W are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. V sits fourth to the left of G. Only three people sit between F and I when counted from the right of I. H sits to the immediate right of F. W is an immediate neighbour of I as well as V. Who sits third to the left of U?
questions.solution:
Place V four left of G, F four right of I and H immediately right of F. W must sit between I and V. Completing the circle places I third left of U.
**Answer: I**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster)
questions.solution:
Three pairs advance each letter by two. FI → JM advances each letter by four, so it is different.
**Answer: FI-JM**

questions.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A × B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is R related to F if ‘R – P + S × N ÷ F'?
questions.solution:
P is the father of S and N, and R is P’s wife. N is F’s mother, so R is F’s maternal grandmother.
**Answer: Mother’s mother**

questions.q: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 91 93 96 101 108 ?
questions.solution:
Add consecutive primes 2, 3, 5 and 7. The next prime is 11, so next term = 108 + 11 = 119.
**Answer: 119**

questions.q: Kartikeyan starts from Point A and drives 37 km towards West. He then takes a right turn, drives 26 km, turns right and drives 42 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 47 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 5 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
questions.solution:
East–west movement cancels: -37 + 42 - 5 = 0. North–south movement leaves him 21 km south of A. He must drive 21 km north.
**Answer: 21 km to the North**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All vultures are sparrows. Some sparrows are crows. No crow is a pigeon. Conclusions: (I) Some vultures are crows. (II) No sparrow is a pigeon.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.solution:
The sparrows that are crows need not include any vultures. Also sparrows outside the crow group may be pigeons. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.
**Answer: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 23 24 28 37 53 ?
questions.solution:
Add successive squares: 1, 4, 9 and 16. Next add 25 to 53, giving 78.
**Answer: 78**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operations on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations, e.g., if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 12 – 36 – 51 – 63; 20 – 60 – 75 – 87
questions.solution:
Multiply the first number by three, add 15, then add 12. The matching set is 25 → 75 → 90 → 102.
**Answer: 25 – 75 – 90 – 102**

questions.q: Each of M, N, O, P, Q, R and S has an flight on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. S has flight on third last day of the week. Only two people have flight between R and S. Only four people have flight between R and Q. P has flight immediately after N. M doesn’t have flight on Monday. On which day does M have a flight?
questions.solution:
S is on Friday, R on Tuesday and Q on Sunday. N and P must take Wednesday and Thursday. M cannot be on Monday, so M’s flight is on Saturday.
**Answer: Saturday**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (7,18,39) (3,19,28)
questions.solution:
The third number equals three times the first plus the second. The set (23, 4, 73) works because 3 × 23 + 4 = 73.
**Answer: (23,4,73)**

questions.q: This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below. (Left) 564 487 769 478 546 (Right) (Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right. What will be the resultant if the second digit of the second highest number is added to the third digit of the lowest number?
questions.solution:
Second highest is 564, whose second digit is 6. Lowest is 478, whose third digit is 8. Sum = 6 + 8 = 14.
**Answer: 14**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster)
questions.solution:
The normal pattern subtracts three alphabet places at each step. URQ subtracts three and then one, so it is the odd cluster.
**Answer: URQ**

questions.q: This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below. (Left) 412 368 457 283 396 (Right) (Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right. What will be the resultant if third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of lowest number ?
questions.solution:
Highest is 457, whose third digit is 7. Lowest is 283, whose second digit is 8. Their sum is 15.
**Answer: 15**

questions.q: In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer. Q. Anita, Bhavna, Charu, Deepa, and Esha, each scored different marks. Who scored the lowest marks? (I) Bhavna scored more than Anita but less than Charu. (II) Deepa scored more than Anita but less than Bhavna.
options: Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
questions.solution:
Together the statements order Charu above Bhavna, Deepa and Anita, but say nothing about Esha. Esha could be below Anita, so the lowest scorer cannot be uniquely identified.
**Answer: Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question**

questions.q: Which of the given letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the following series to make it logically complete? LEF 11 ATU 22 PIJ 33 EXY 44 ?
questions.solution:
Every letter advances fifteen places modulo the alphabet and the number increases by eleven. EXY 44 is followed by TMN 55.
**Answer: TMN 55**
